payload.prompt: Create an order for the customer Brightstone Ltd (org no. 971948981) with the products Data Advisory (4083) at 4050 NOK and Training Session (7105) at 12150 NOK. Convert the order to an invoice and register full payment.

payload.goal: Create an order for Brightstone Ltd with two products, convert the order to an invoice, and register full payment.
success_checks: Customer Brightstone Ltd (org no. 971948981) exists in the system
Product 'Data Advisory' (product number 4083) exists with unit price 4050 NOK
Product 'Training Session' (product number 7105) exists with unit price 12150 NOK
Order is created with both line items correctly attached
Order is successfully converted to an invoice
Full payment of 16200 NOK (excl. VAT) or 20250 NOK (incl. 25% VAT) is registered against the invoice
Invoice status reflects as fully paid
risk_notes: VAT rate not explicitly stated; defaulting to 25% as standard Norwegian VAT (mva) — verify if any line item is VAT-exempt
Customer Brightstone Ltd may not exist in the sandbox; must be created before order creation
Products 4083 and 7105 may not exist; must be created before order lines are added
No invoice date or payment due date specified; system defaults will be used
No payment method or bank account specified; bank account must be configured for payment registration
Organization number 971948981 should be validated as a valid Norwegian org number
payload.suggested_first_action: Look up or create customer Brightstone Ltd with org no. 971948981 via POST /customer
ordered_steps: 1. Ensure bank account is configured in Tripletex (required for payment registration)
2. Create or verify customer Brightstone Ltd via POST /customer with organizationNumber=971948981
3. Create or verify product 'Data Advisory' via POST /product with number=4083, price=4050
4. Create or verify product 'Training Session' via POST /product with number=7105, price=12150
5. Create order via POST /order with customerId referencing Brightstone Ltd
6. Add order line for Data Advisory via POST /orderline with orderId, productId for 4083, quantity=1, unitPriceExcludingVat=4050, vatPercent=25
7. Add order line for Training Session via POST /orderline with orderId, productId for 7105, quantity=1, unitPriceExcludingVat=12150, vatPercent=25
8. Convert order to invoice via PUT /order/{id}/:invoice to generate invoice from the order
9. Retrieve the generated invoice ID from the response
10. Register full payment via POST /ledger/payment or POST /invoice/{id}/:payment with full amount (20250 NOK incl. 25% VAT) against the invoice
11. Verify invoice status is 'PAID' via GET /invoice/{id}

planned_endpoints.summary: Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.
Create new invoice or subscription invoice from order.

rules: When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.

payload.headline: Perfect run: all 5 checks passed with 10 API calls and 0 errors.
what_worked: All 5 scoring checks passed with zero 4xx errors, achieving a perfect 8.0/8.0 raw score.
Efficient use of batch endpoint POST /order/orderline/list to add both lines in a single call.
what_to_try_next: Eliminate the two separate GET /product calls (one per product) by trusting the execution brief which already confirms product IDs — saves 2 calls.
Skip GET /ledger/account and GET /invoice/paymentType if the brief already provides bank account and payment type info, reducing calls by 2 more.
Consider combining bank account setup (PUT /ledger/account) with order creation in parallel rather than sequentially to reduce wall-clock time, though call count stays the same.
unnecessary_calls: GET /product (x2) — product IDs 84411997 and 84411999 were already known from the brief; these lookups added no new info.
GET /invoice/paymentType — payment type could be assumed or cached from prior runs; this lookup was not strictly needed.
